title: Affiliate, marketplace and retail media
purpose: When an affiliate payout, an ad invoice or an Amazon ad bill is due, open Affiliate, marketplace and retail media to pay partners and platforms only for sales they truly caused and to hand whoever runs Amazon a brief built on profit.
fires: the network's one-click approve, the bookkeeper's month-end scramble, the Amazon agency's sales-only report, and paying invoices unread
not_for: a brand with no affiliate program, no marketplace ads and a small single-platform ad bill

jobs.job: When the affiliate network's payout is due Friday, tell me which commissions are for orders that were returned, cancelled or never real, so I pay only for sales that happened and stayed
jobs.circumstance: Wednesday, the network's payout request is $14,000, the approve button is one click, nobody has matched it to store orders

progress.functional: match every commission claimed to a kept store order and hold the rest
progress.emotional: stop the uneasy feeling of signing off money I have not checked
progress.social: show the bookkeeper and partner that payouts are checked, not waved through

jobs.hire_today: nothing; most brands press approve because matching network reports to store orders by hand takes a day
jobs.fire: the one-click approve and the network's own verified column

forces.push: commission on returned or fake orders comes straight out of profit
forces.pull: a payout list with each commission marked kept, returned, cancelled or not found
forces.habit: the network verifies it, so it must be right
forces.anxiety: what if holding a payout upsets a good partner

watch.metric: commission claimed against commission on verified, kept orders, each payout cycle

drives.metric: affiliate commission as a share of affiliate revenue, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $14,000 claimed, $2,100 on orders later returned or cancelled. After: $11,900 paid, the rest held with a reason.
jobs.not_for: a brand with no affiliate program, or one paying fewer than 10 partners a month

jobs.job: When the Amazon agency reports record ad sales but the Amazon payout barely moved, tell me what the ads cost against profit after Amazon fees, so I stop growing sales that lose money
jobs.circumstance: monthly agency call, ad sales up 40 percent, net payout from Amazon up 5 percent

progress.functional: ad cost per unit against profit per unit after all Amazon fees, by product
progress.emotional: stop the confusion of good sales and bad profit
progress.social: hold the agency to profit, not sales, and look sharp doing it

jobs.hire_today: the Amazon agency's report, or a freelancer

forces.push: every month at the wrong target costs margin on every unit
forces.pull: a break-even ad cost per product after fees, with the products above it
forces.habit: the agency optimises for sales, as agreed
forces.anxiety: what if cutting spend loses rank and organic sales

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and before any agency review

watch.metric: Amazon ad cost of sales against break-even after fees, trailing 30 days
watch.source: Amazon Ads console and Seller Central

drives.metric: Amazon profit after ads and fees, monthly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: ads run at 38 percent of sales against a 24 percent break-even. After: 22 percent in 60 days, profit after ads up $6,000 a month.
jobs.not_for: a brand not selling on Amazon, or selling on Amazon with no ads
